_meta.author: Eduventure (original questions)
_meta.note: Secondary batch: lower secondary 25 (Maths 10, Science 8, History 4, Bahasa Melayu 3) and upper secondary 25 (Maths, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, English: 5 each). In review until approved in /admin. Contains answers: never imported by src/.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Evaluate 2³ × 3².

mistakes.why: 36 comes from 2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 2 = 6. Powers mean repeated multiplication: 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 and 3² = 9.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: squares, cubes and indices (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Simplify 6a + 2b − 4a + b.
questions.explanation: Collect like terms: 6a − 4a = 2a and 2b + b = 3b.

wrong.c: b on its own means 1b, so 2b + b = 3b.
wrong.d: Unlike terms (a and b) cannot be combined into one term.

questions.objective: Simplify expressions by collecting like terms.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: algebraic expressions (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Solve for x: x/4 + 3 = 7
questions.explanation: Subtract 3: x/4 = 4. Multiply by 4: x = 16.

mistakes.why: Undo ÷ 4 by multiplying by 4, not dividing.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: linear equations (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is the cube root of 125?
questions.explanation: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so the cube root of 125 is 5.

mistakes.why: 25 × 25 × 25 is far more than 125; the cube root is the number that multiplies by itself three times to give 125.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: squares, square roots, cubes and cube roots (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Which point lies on the y-axis?
questions.explanation: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0.

wrong.b: (5, 0) has y = 0, so it lies on the x-axis.
wrong.c: (5, 5) is in the first quadrant, away from both axes.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: coordinates (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: RM60 is shared between Mei and Raj in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does Raj get, in ringgit?
questions.explanation: There are 2 + 3 = 5 parts, so one part is 60 ÷ 5 = RM12. Raj gets 3 parts: 3 × 12 = RM36.

mistakes.why: Divide by the total number of parts (5), not by 3.

questions.objective: Share an amount in a given ratio.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: ratio, rate and proportion (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: A bus travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 km/h.

mistakes.why: 375 is distance × time; speed divides distance by time.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: speed and acceleration (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Select all the values of x that satisfy x + 2 > 5.
questions.explanation: x + 2 > 5 means x > 3. So 4, 7 and 10 work.

wrong.b: 3 + 2 = 5, which equals 5 but is not greater than 5.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: linear inequalities (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: the circumference of a circle equals π multiplied by its diameter.
questions.explanation: C = πd, which is the same as C = 2πr because the diameter is twice the radius.

wrong.false: π is defined as circumference ÷ diameter, so C = πd for every circle.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: circles (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Put these lengths in order from shortest to longest.
questions.explanation: Convert to centimetres: 95 cm, 0.001 km = 100 cm, 1,100 mm = 110 cm, 1.2 m = 120 cm.
questions.objective: Convert and compare metric units of length.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary mathematics: measurement (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters it?
questions.explanation: The iris is the coloured ring that widens or narrows the pupil: smaller in bright light, bigger in dim light.

wrong.b: The lens focuses light onto the retina.
wrong.c: The retina detects light and forms the image.
wrong.d: The optic nerve carries signals from the retina to the brain.

questions.objective: Describe the parts of the eye and their functions.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: sense organs (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 1–2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A ray of light hits a flat mirror with an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The law of reflection: the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, both measured from the normal.

mistakes.why: 60° is measured from the mirror surface; angles are measured from the normal line.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: light (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Select all the mixtures.
questions.explanation: A mixture contains different substances that are not chemically joined: air (several gases), seawater (water and salts) and soil.

wrong.c: Pure water is a compound: hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: matter (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 1–2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: True or false: light travels in straight lines.
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines, which is why shadows form behind opaque objects.

wrong.false: Shadows show that light cannot bend around objects on its own: it travels in straight lines (until it is reflected or refracted).

questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: light (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Match each separation method to the job it does best.

right.text: Getting pure water from salt water

questions.explanation: Filtration traps insoluble solids, distillation boils and condenses the liquid, and chromatography separates dissolved substances that travel at different speeds.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: matter (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the main job of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: White blood cells protect the body by destroying germs and making antibodies.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: blood circulation (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Put these planets in order, starting with the one closest to the Sun.
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars: the four rocky inner planets.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: the solar system (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 3).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What instrument is used to measure electric current?
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures current in amperes (A) and is connected in series. A voltmeter measures voltage and is connected in parallel.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary science: electricity (e.g. KSSM Sains Tingkatan 3).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: Who founded Melaka?
questions.explanation: Parameswara, a prince from Palembang, founded Melaka around 1400.

wrong.b: Hang Tuah was a famous warrior (laksamana) in Melaka's later years.
wrong.c: Tun Perak was a great Bendahara who helped Melaka grow.
wrong.d: Sultan Mansur Shah ruled Melaka later, at the height of its power.

questions.alignment: Lower secondary history: the Melaka Sultanate (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: In which year did the Portuguese capture Melaka?
questions.explanation: The Portuguese, led by Alfonso de Albuquerque, captured Melaka in 1511.

mistakes.why: 1641 is when the Dutch took Melaka from the Portuguese.

questions.objective: Recall key dates in the history of Melaka.
questions.alignment: Lower secondary history: the Melaka Sultanate (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 2).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: Put the powers that ruled Melaka in order, earliest first.
questions.explanation: Melaka Sultanate (from about 1400) → Portuguese (1511) → Dutch (1641) → British (from 1824).
questions.alignment: Lower secondary history: Melaka and colonial powers (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 2–3).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: Which early civilisation grew up along the River Nile?
questions.explanation: Ancient Egypt depended on the Nile's yearly floods, which left fertile soil for farming.

wrong.b: Mesopotamia grew between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
wrong.c: The Indus Valley civilisation grew along the Indus River.
wrong.d: Early Chinese civilisation grew along the Huang He (Yellow River).

questions.alignment: Lower secondary history: early civilisations (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 1).

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Apakah maksud peribahasa "bagai aur dengan tebing"?
questions.explanation: Aur (buluh) menahan tebing daripada runtuh, dan tebing menjadi tempat aur tumbuh. Peribahasa ini bermaksud saling membantu.

wrong.b: Bermusuhan ialah lawan maksud peribahasa ini.
wrong.c: Peribahasa ini tidak berkaitan dengan sifat sombong.
wrong.d: Peribahasa ini tidak berkaitan dengan sifat malas.

questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu sekolah menengah rendah: peribahasa (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Melayu).

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Lengkapkan dengan bentuk kata kerja yang betul bagi "tulis": Kakak sedang ___ surat.
questions.explanation: Awalan meN- + tulis menjadi "menulis" (huruf t digugurkan dan diganti dengan n).
questions.objective: Menggunakan imbuhan awalan meN- dengan betul.
questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu sekolah menengah rendah: tatabahasa (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Melayu).

questions.subject: malay_language
questions.prompt: Betul atau salah: perkataan "cantik" ialah kata adjektif.
questions.explanation: Kata adjektif menerangkan sifat kata nama. "Cantik" menerangkan sifat, contohnya "bunga yang cantik".

wrong.false: "Cantik" menerangkan rupa atau sifat sesuatu, jadi ia ialah kata adjektif, bukan kata nama atau kata kerja.

questions.alignment: Bahasa Melayu sekolah menengah rendah: tatabahasa (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Melayu).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Using π = 22/7, find the length of an arc with radius 7 cm and angle 90° at the centre, in cm.

mistakes.why: 44 cm is the whole circumference; 90° is a quarter of the circle.
38.5 cm² is the sector's area, not the arc length.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: circles (e.g. KSSM Matematik / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that both land heads?
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. One of four is HH, so P = 1/4 (= 1/2 × 1/2).

wrong.b: 1/2 is the chance for one coin; for both, multiply: 1/2 × 1/2.
wrong.c: There are four equally likely outcomes, not three: HT and TH are different.
wrong.d: 2/4 is the chance of exactly one head.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: probability of combined events (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: A speed–time graph shows a car moving at a constant 20 m/s for 10 s. What distance does it travel, in metres?
questions.explanation: Distance = area under the speed–time graph = 20 × 10 = 200 m.

mistakes.why: Distance is speed × time, not speed ÷ time.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: graphs of motion (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: a line parallel to the x-axis has a gradient of 0.
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has no vertical change: gradient = rise ÷ run = 0 ÷ run = 0.

wrong.false: A horizontal line does not rise at all, so its gradient is 0. (It is a vertical line whose gradient is undefined.)

questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: straight lines (e.g. KSSM Matematik / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is the exact value of tan 45°?
questions.explanation: In a right-angled isosceles triangle, the opposite and adjacent sides are equal, so tan 45° = opposite ÷ adjacent = 1.

mistakes.why: About 0.707 is sin 45° or cos 45°; tan 45° = 1.

questions.objective: Recall trigonometric ratios of special angles.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: trigonometry (e.g. KSSM Matematik / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: What is the weight of a 60 kg person on Earth, taking g = 10 N/kg, in newtons?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × gravitational field strength = 60 × 10 = 600 N.

mistakes.why: 60 kg is the mass; weight is a force, W = mg.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: gravitation (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which lens is used to correct short-sightedness (myopia)?
questions.explanation: A short-sighted eye focuses distant light in front of the retina. A concave lens spreads the light out so it focuses on the retina.

wrong.c: A mirror reflects light; it cannot be worn to focus vision.
wrong.d: A prism bends and splits light; it does not correct focus.

questions.objective: Explain how lenses correct vision defects.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: light and optics (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: How much energy, in joules, is needed to heat 2 kg of water by 10 °C? (Specific heat capacity of water = 4,200 J/kg °C.)

mistakes.why: Include the mass: 2 kg doubles the energy needed.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: heat (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Select all the units of energy.
questions.explanation: Joules, kilowatt-hours (used on electricity bills) and electronvolts (used in atomic physics) all measure energy.

wrong.c: The watt measures power: energy per second.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: energy (e.g. KSSM Fizik / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: True or false: a transformer works with direct current (d.c.).
questions.explanation: A transformer needs a changing magnetic field to induce a voltage in the secondary coil. Steady d.c. makes a constant field, so nothing is induced.

wrong.true: Induction needs a changing magnetic field, which only alternating current provides continuously.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: electromagnetism (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which of these is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: A strong acid ionises completely in water. Hydrochloric acid does; the others only partly ionise.

wrong.b: Ethanoic acid (in vinegar) is a weak acid.
wrong.c: Carbonic acid (in fizzy drinks) is a weak acid.
wrong.d: Citric acid (in citrus fruit) is a weak acid.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: acids, bases and salts (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A sodium atom has 11 electrons. How many electrons does a sodium ion, Na⁺, have?
questions.explanation: Na⁺ forms when a sodium atom loses one electron: 11 − 1 = 10.

mistakes.why: A positive ion has lost electrons, not gained them.

questions.objective: Work out the electrons in ions.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: chemical bonds (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Match each alloy to its main metal.
questions.explanation: Bronze is mostly copper (with tin), steel is mostly iron (with carbon), duralumin is mostly aluminium (with copper and other metals).
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: manufactured substances in industry (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Put these metals in order of reactivity, most reactive first.
questions.explanation: Potassium reacts violently with water, magnesium burns brightly, iron rusts slowly and copper is quite unreactive.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: redox and reactivity series (e.g. KSSM Kimia / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: An acid reacts with an alkali to form a salt and which other substance?
questions.explanation: Neutralisation: acid + alkali → salt + water. For example, HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: acids, bases and salts (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which organelle makes proteins?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes join amino acids together to build proteins, following instructions carried by mRNA.

wrong.b: The nucleus holds the DNA instructions but does not assemble proteins.
wrong.c: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins after they are made.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: cell structure (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: How many chromosomes are there in a normal human body cell?
questions.explanation: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs. Sperm and egg cells have 23.

mistakes.why: 23 is the number of pairs, or the number in a sperm or egg cell.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: inheritance (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Select all the abiotic (non-living) factors in an ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are physical and chemical conditions: temperature, light and soil pH.

wrong.c: Predators are living, so they are a biotic factor.
wrong.e: Bacteria are living organisms: a biotic factor.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: ecosystems (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: True or false: arteries have thinner walls than veins.
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood at high pressure straight from the heart, so they have thick, muscular, elastic walls. Veins carry blood at low pressure and have thinner walls.

wrong.true: It is the other way round: high pressure in arteries needs thick walls.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: transport in humans (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Put these parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them.
questions.explanation: Mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine (most absorption) → large intestine (water absorbed).
questions.objective: Trace the path of food through the digestive system.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: nutrition and digestion (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Change to reported speech: She said, "I am tired."

options.text: She said that she was tired.
She said that I am tired.
She said that she is being tired.
She says that she was tired.

questions.explanation: In reported speech after "said", the tense usually moves back (am → was) and the pronoun changes (I → she).

wrong.b: The pronoun must change: she is talking about herself, so "I" becomes "she".
wrong.c: "Is being tired" is not natural English; the tense moves back to "was".
wrong.d: The reporting verb should stay in the past: she said.

questions.objective: Convert direct speech to reported speech.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary English: reported speech (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Inggeris / CEFR B1–B2).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the third conditional correctly?

options.text: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I studied, I would have passed.
If I would have studied, I would pass.
If I have studied, I will pass.

questions.explanation: The third conditional talks about an imagined past: If + past perfect (had studied), would have + past participle (would have passed).

wrong.b: The if-clause needs the past perfect: had studied.
wrong.c: "Would" does not go in the if-clause.
wrong.d: This mixes present perfect and future; it is not a past regret.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary English: conditionals (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Inggeris / CEFR B2).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Select all the sentences that are in the passive voice.

options.text: The cake was eaten by the children.
They are building a new bridge.

questions.explanation: Passive sentences use a form of "be" + past participle, and the subject receives the action: was eaten, has been sent.

wrong.c: "She wrote" is active: the subject does the action.

questions.alignment: Upper secondary English: active and passive voice (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Inggeris / CEFR B1–B2).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Match each linking word to its purpose.
questions.explanation: "However" introduces a contrast, "therefore" a result, and "furthermore" an additional point.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary English: writing (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Inggeris / SPM).

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Write the noun form of the verb "decide".
questions.explanation: decide (verb) → decision (noun): "It was a difficult decision."
questions.alignment: Upper secondary English: vocabulary (e.g. KSSM Bahasa Inggeris / CEFR B1–B2).
